h: Rare Breeds and a Mystery in Wax
p: Stow Bardolph has a quirky claim to fame just a short walk from the farm, and it's one for the history fans. In the village church of Holy Trinity, the Hare family chapel holds a wax effigy of Sarah Hare, who died in the 1740s and left instructions in her will for her likeness to be made. It sits in a mahogany cupboard and is one of the more unusual things you'll find in an English parish church. Slightly spooky, completely fascinating, and older kids tend to love it.

Back on the farm, the rare breeds angle gives you a brilliant game to play. Ask the kids to spot animals they've never seen in a picture book, then read the signs together to find out where each breed comes from. Plenty of traditional British breeds are named after places, so you can turn it into a little geography lesson without anybody noticing. Bring a bag for any farm shop goodies and a bit of change in case there's animal feed on offer.

The countryside round here is classic Fenland, flat as a pancake and criss-crossed with drains and rivers. Denver Sluice, just south of Downham Market, is a big piece of engineering that helps control the water levels of the Great Ouse, and it's an interesting spot for a short walk. Wildlife fans should also know that the Ouse Washes are famous for winter swans, with the WWT centre at Welney a short drive away. It all makes for a gentle, big-sky day where the farm is just the start.
